name: attributed to Retired Emperor Kazan
bio: The Shūi wakashū (Collection of Gleanings) is the third imperial anthology of Japanese waka, completed around 1005 to 1007 in the reign of Emperor Ichijō. Tradition ascribes the compilation to the Retired Emperor Kazan (968–1008), himself a poet, though the attribution is uncertain and the work may rest on an earlier private collection.

Its twenty books follow the pattern of the Kokin wakashū and the Gosen wakashū: the seasons, congratulation, parting, hidden-word poems, miscellany, Kagura songs, love and grief. This page carries the work itself; the individual poems are credited to their many authors only in the source, not here.
